what_happened: The operator ran the CI-routing build (job s6tr) directly, ahead of the order in Athena's plan. The owner's top priority was speed (2026-10-16 addendum), but the plan put the speed work last because every rung of the plan defaulted to implementation. The operator overrode the plan's order and filed a gap.
cause: Planning treats every rung as the same kind of work and sequences by default, not by the owner's stated priority. Owner priorities from addenda are not an input to plan ordering, and there is no check that the plan's order matches the latest stated priority. The queue has no priority support either (see the earlier drain case), so the only way to change order is an operator bypass.
prevention: Make owner priority a first-class field. Record it from requests and addenda, and have the planner sort rungs by it before the default order. Add a code check that fails plan creation when the top stated priority is not in the first position or has no rationale for its position. The queue and drain should also honor this priority, so no operator bypass is needed.
proposed_request: Make Athena's planner and queue respect the owner's stated priority. Record priorities from requests and addenda, such as the 2026-10-16 speed addendum, as a field on the plan and on queue items. Order plan rungs and queue drains by that priority first, then by the existing default order. Reject or flag a plan whose highest-priority item is not placed first unless it gives a reason. Show that a plan with a speed priority and default implementation rungs puts the speed work (such as the CI-routing build) first, with no operator reordering.
